dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Texans (4-6) Week 12 Briefing: Wednesday Injury Report Ahead of Ravens
bullets: Roster & Front Office: Houston signed DT Junior Tafuna and WR Daniel Sobkowicz to the practice squad [Pro Football Rumors](https://www.profootballrumors.com/2026/11/nfl-practice-squad-updates-11-25-26).

Injury & Practice Status: DE Logan Hall (hip / shoulder) and WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) logged limited practice reps Wednesday [houstontexans.com Official](https://www.houstontexans.com/news/week-12-injury-report-texans-vs-ravens). DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring), TE Brevin Jordan (finger / foot), WR Kayshon Boutte (hip), and DT Sheldon Rankins (ankle) did not practice Wednesday, while RB Woody Marks (concussion) and LB Jake Hansen (elbow) practiced in full [houstontexans.com Official](https://www.houstontexans.com/news/week-12-injury-report-texans-vs-ravens).

Week 12 Ravens Outlook: DeMeco Ryans and DC Matt Burke open installation for the Baltimore Ravens (4-7, HOU -6.5, HC Jesse Minter, OC Declan Doyle & DC Anthony Weaver (NRG Stadium)) as Houston prepares for a pivotal AFC matchup [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/preview?gameId=401873085) [houstontexans.com Official](https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-participate-in-nfl-s-2026-my-cause-my-cleats-initiative).

AFC Playoff Trajectory: Entering Week 12 at 4-6 (2nd in AFC South • #9 Seed in AFC), Houston carries a 23.2% postseason projection, 6.2% AFC South division title mark, and 0% #1 Seed Bye equity into the conference stretch [fizzyjoe](https://www.battleredblog.com/houston-texans-power-rankings/79275/houston-texans-nfl-power-rankings-week-12).

Statistical Profile & Matchup Edge: Through Week 11, Houston ranks #9 in Points / Game (25.9), #16 in Points Allowed / Game (22.2), #9 in Turnover Differential (+4), giving DeMeco Ryans and Matt Burke a clear benchmark ahead of Sun, Nov 29, 12:00 PM CST • NFL TV at [object Object] against the Baltimore Ravens [Scott Barzilla](https://www.battleredblog.com/houston-texans-analysis/79219/value-of-things-by-the-numbers).

rawStream.fullText:
All 33 designed runs by the Texans vs. the Colts.

By far the Texans best run-blocking performance of the season, earning an 86.7 PFF run-blocking grade. Their previous season high was 67.6.

Both David Montgomery and Emari Demercado looked good, but it starts up front.

I know the opponent needs to be taken into consideration, but outside of the Browns game, I do feel like the Texans run blocking has started to trend in the right direction as of late, also Braden Smith makes a big difference.

Getting back to the 1-2 punch of Montgomery and Woody Marks, while now having what appears to be a viable third option in Demercado, could be huge for this offense down the stretch.

We'll see how much of that improvement was opponent-driven, but certainly encouraging to see.
